It is a Jerusalem Cross. It is also referred to as the Crusader's Cross. It is a large Greek cross surrounded by 4 smaller versions. It originated in the 11th century and was later used as the coats of arms of the Crusaders, and as the seal of the rulers of Jerusalem. There are different interpretations as to the meaning of this cross. The most popular ones are listed below.

1 - The central cross stands for Christ and the four smaller crosses stand for the 4 evangelists of John, Luke, Mark, and Matthew

2 - The large cross represents Christ as the strength at the center of Christianity and the smaller crosses as the 4 corners of the earth

to which the faith spread.

3 - The crosses represent the wounds that Christ suffered when He was crucified; the central cross for the wound on His side, and the 4 smaller crosses for the wounds on His hands and feet
